title: Photoreduction of Cerium(IV) in Ce2(OiPr)8(iPrOH)2. Characterization and Structure of Ce4O(OiPr)13(iPrOH)

synthesis.procedure: All manipulations under dry N2 or Ar or in vacuo with dried, distilled solvents stored under N2. A solution of Ce2(OiPr)8(iPrOH)2 (10 g) in 2:1 MeOC2H4OMe/iPrOH (50 mL) was exposed to sunlight for 50 h (not optimized). The color changed to olive green then orange-brown. Storage of the reaction solution at −30 °C for 48 h gave orange-brown crystals (3.3 g, 41%). The product is very air-sensitive (dark color changes to yellow within 10 s in air).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: sunlight photolysis of solution under inert atmosphere
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After photolysis, the reaction solution was stored at −30 °C for 48 h to give orange-brown crystals.

properties.summary: Mixed-valence Ce(III)/Ce(IV) butterfly cluster is paramagnetic. SQUID susceptibility (5–300 K; 0.5 and 2.0 T, no field dependence) shows two Curie–Weiss regimes: μeff = 2.70 μB (80–300 K) and 1.83 μB (5–40 K). Powder EPR at 4 K is complex; major features assigned as g∥ = 2.41 and g⊥ = 1.64 (gav = 1.90), predicting μeff = 1.65 for an S = 1/2 species, accounting for most of the susceptibility.

measurements.name: EPR g values (major species)
measurements.conditions: X-band powder EPR at ~4 K; features B and C in Figure 1; predicted μeff = 1.65 for S = 1/2

source_locations.location: Experimental Section, synthesis and elemental analysis (C42H99Ce4O15)
